questions.prompt: An NMOS has \(V_{T0} = 0.4\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\gamma = 0.5\ \mathrm{V^{1/2}}\), \(-2\varphi_p = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\). Find \(V_T\) in V at \(V_{SB} = 1\ \mathrm{V}\).
questions.explanation: \(V_T = V_{T0} + \gamma(\sqrt{-2\varphi_p + V_{SB}} - \sqrt{-2\varphi_p}) = 0.4 + 0.5(1.304 - 0.837) = 0.634\ \mathrm{V}\) (reader Eq. 10.12). Using \(\gamma\sqrt{V_{SB}}\) alone gives 0.9 V.
questions.figure_alt: Threshold voltage versus source-to-body voltage: V_T starts at V_T0 when V_SB = 0 and rises along a square-root-shaped curve as V_SB increases.

questions.prompt: Why does a positive \(V_{SB}\) raise an NMOS threshold?
options: It widens the depletion region under the channel, so more bulk charge must be balanced before inversion
questions.explanation: The body acts as a back gate through \(C_{dep}\). Reverse body bias adds depletion charge \(|Q_B|\), which the gate must support first, so \(V_T\) rises.
questions.figure_alt: Threshold voltage versus source-to-body voltage: V_T starts at V_T0 when V_SB = 0 and rises along a square-root-shaped curve as V_SB increases.

questions.prompt: How is the body transconductance defined?
questions.explanation: Raising the body (lower \(V_{SB}\)) lowers \(V_T\) and increases current, so \(\partial I_D/\partial V_{BS} > 0\). The chain rule through \(V_T\) gives the factor \(\eta = \partial V_T/\partial V_{SB}\) (Eq. 10.17).

questions.explanation: \(\eta = 0.4/(2\sqrt{1.3}) = 0.175\), so \(g_{mb} = 0.351\ \mathrm{mS}\). Using \(\sqrt{V_{SB}}\) alone in the denominator gives 0.566 mS.

questions.prompt: In which configuration does the body effect play no role at all?
options: Any NMOS with its body at ground
Source and body tied together, so \(V_{SB} = 0\) and \(v_{bs} = 0\)
questions.explanation: With the body at ground, a source above ground still has \(V_{SB} > 0\) and any source signal creates \(v_{bs}\). Only tying source to body removes both.

questions.prompt: An NMOS with \(\gamma = 0.45\ \mathrm{V^{1/2}}\), \(-2\varphi_p = 0.75\ \mathrm{V}\) has its source lifted to 1.2 V above the grounded body. By how many mV must \(V_{GS}\) increase to keep the same current?
questions.explanation: Same current needs the same overdrive, so \(V_{GS}\) rises by \(\Delta V_T = 0.45(\sqrt{1.95} - \sqrt{0.75}) = 0.45(1.396 - 0.866) = 239\ \mathrm{mV}\).
questions.figure_alt: Threshold voltage versus source-to-body voltage: V_T starts at V_T0 when V_SB = 0 and rises along a square-root-shaped curve as V_SB increases.

questions.prompt: Where does the body source sit in the four-terminal small-signal model?
options: From drain to body, controlled by \(v_{gs}\)
A second controlled source \(g_{mb}v_{bs}\) from drain to source, in parallel with \(g_mv_{gs}\)
questions.explanation: Both front and back gates modulate the same channel current, so both sources sit between drain and source: \(i_d = g_mv_{gs} + g_{mb}v_{bs} + v_{ds}/r_o\) (Eq. 10.18).

questions.prompt: For \(\gamma = 0.4\ \mathrm{V^{1/2}}\) and \(-2\varphi_p = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\), at what \(V_{SB}\) (V) does \(\eta = g_{mb}/g_m\) fall to 0.1?
questions.explanation: \(0.4/(2\sqrt{0.7 + V_{SB}}) = 0.1\) gives \(\sqrt{0.7 + V_{SB}} = 2\), so \(V_{SB} = 3.3\ \mathrm{V}\). The body effect weakens as reverse bias grows, because the depletion capacitance shrinks.
questions.figure_alt: Threshold voltage versus source-to-body voltage: V_T starts at V_T0 when V_SB = 0 and rises along a square-root-shaped curve as V_SB increases.

questions.prompt: In an n-well CMOS process, how can a PMOS avoid the body effect?
options: Put it in its own n-well tied to its source
questions.explanation: A separate well lets body follow source, so \(V_{SB} = 0\) and \(v_{bs} = 0\). NMOS devices share the p-substrate and usually cannot do this. A grounded n-well would forward-bias the source junction.

questions.explanation: \(1/1.2 = 0.833\). The source moves with the input, so \(v_{bs} = -v_{out}\) and the body source fights the output.

A PMOS follower in its own well tied to its source
Either; body effect cannot be avoided
questions.explanation: Removing \(g_{mb}\) removes the gain loss. A larger \(V_{SB}\) only reduces \(\eta\) a little.
